# Pilot — Seattle City Council (Legistar)

**Real data.** Generated by `tools/adapters/legistar.py` from the live Legistar Web API,
which runs the legislative record for a large share of North American cities.

```bash
python3 tools/adapters/legistar.py --client seattle --meetings 8 \
  --utc-offset=-07:00 --out examples/pilot-seattle-meetings
```

8 meetings, 76 agenda items, 27 recorded votes, 7 councilmembers, 32 matters.

## Why this profile needed testing most

`meetings` is the most intricate profile and its vote model was invented from Popolo with
no real-world contact. It held up better than expected — but real data still broke it in
one place and exposed three things the model cannot represent.

### `position` was integer-only

Legistar agenda numbers are strings: `"3."`, `"A."`, `"2a."`. `schema:position` ranges
over **Integer or Text**, so restricting it to integer was simply wrong, and it made all
76 real agenda items unrepresentable. Widened to match schema.org.

## What Legistar does not publish

These are reported by the adapter rather than invented:

**`requiredMajority` — 27 votes affected.** The profile treats this as important, because
without it a reader cannot tell whether a 4-3 vote carried. Legistar has no field for it.
The threshold is real but lives in the body's rules of procedure, not the meeting record.

**Timezone — every meeting.** `EventDate` is `2026-08-21T00:00:00` and `EventTime` is the
separate string `9:30 AM`. Neither carries an offset. The adapter takes one via
`--utc-offset`; a real deployment would read it from the jurisdiction's `gs:timeZone`,
which `_core` already carries. A meeting time without an offset is ambiguous, and this is
the most widely deployed municipal meeting system in North America.

**Location as a resolvable place — every meeting.** `EventLocation` is a multi-line
address string, so there is nothing to resolve a `_core` Facility from.

**Jurisdiction — entirely absent.** Legistar publishes no jurisdiction metadata, so the
adapter derives a minimal one from the client name and marks its identifier `local:`
because it is inferred rather than sourced.

## Client-configured vocabularies

Legistar action and vote labels are configured per city, not fixed by the platform. The
first run surfaced `confirmed`, `discussed`, `heard in Committee` and `Absent(NV)`. Rather
than accumulate spelling variants, labels are normalised — punctuation and parenthetical
qualifiers stripped — before matching. Anything still unrecognised is reported, never
guessed.

## The chain, end to end

```
Human Services, Labor and Economic Development Committee, 2026-08-21
  startDate  2026-08-21T09:30:00-07:00
  item  "3."  An ordinance relating to domestic worker labor standards  [adopted]
    about -> CB 121266 (ordinance)
    vote  -> passed (yes=4)
      Alexis Mercedes Rinck · Dionne Foster · Joy Hollingsworth · Rob Saka
```

Meeting to agenda item to vote to named councilmember, and the same item to the
legislation it concerns — the `meetings`-to-`code` join, exercised against a real
publisher rather than a fixture.
